claim: The repository is a React/Vite browser calculator app with standard, scientific, unit-conversion, financial, and graphing modes.
notes: The entry HTML, app shell, and package manifest all indicate a client-side calculator experience.

claim: The root App component coordinates state, mode selection, keyboard handling, history, theme, sound, and modal/drawer composition.
notes: This is the architectural center of the application.

claim: Shared calculator math, formatting, unit conversion, and financial helpers are centralized in src/utils/evaluator.js.
notes: This module is shared by multiple UI modes.

claim: The grapher mode uses mathjs compilation and canvas rendering for user-entered functions.
notes: The grapher is the most browser-specific feature in the repository.

claim: The app persists theme, sound, and history data in browser localStorage.
notes: Client-side persistence is a key trust boundary and change surface.

claim: The history drawer can export a text file from the browser using Blob and download link logic.
notes: This is a browser-only workflow and a relevant security surface.

claim: The repository declares Vite build and lint scripts in package.json.
notes: The package manifest is the source of the standard validation commands.

claim: ESLint is configured for the React/Vite app and the repository currently reports lint issues in several components.
notes: Legacy lint state is part of the development story and should be surfaced to agents.

claim: The repository currently lacks a test script and test files, so automated regression coverage is absent.
notes: This absence is a key risk for future changes.

claim: The feature-specific UI modules are organized under src/components.
notes: The component tree is the feature composition layer.

claim: The browser entry point is the HTML document that mounts the React app.
notes: This is the document root for the app.

claim: The main React bootstrap module mounts the app inside StrictMode.
notes: This is the runtime bootstrap path.
